behavior: Social and colonial; rests and nests in flocks on open ground. Forages by flying low over calm water with the elongated lower mandible slicing the surface, snapping the bill shut when it contacts a small fish. Active by day and often at dusk or night; calls are short, barking notes.
field_marks: Long, blade-thin red-orange and black bill, with the lower mandible projecting well beyond the upper
Jet-black cap and upperparts sharply contrasting with a white forehead, neck, and underparts
Very long, pointed wings and sleek, low-slung tern-like proportions
Short red-orange legs with webbed feet
Dark eye set inconspicuously in the black cap, with a narrow vertical pupil
habitat: Open sandy beaches, islands, shell or gravel bars, mudflats, estuaries, lagoons, sheltered bays, coastal marshes, and broad rivers or large inland lakes. Nesting sites are sparsely vegetated open ground near productive shallow water.
